problem: The build command ends with two dots: docker build -t registry.example.com/shop:${SHA} .. — the second dot makes the build context the parent directory, so the Dockerfile in the project folder is not used as intended. The command as written is wrong.
fix: docker build -t registry.example.com/shop:${SHA} . (single dot as the build context)

problem: The answer command has no image name: docker run -p 8080:3000 . — read literally, the image would be ".", which is not an image. The port mapping is right but the command is incomplete/wrong.
fix: docker run -p 8080:3000 shop (host port 8080 first, container port 3000 second, then the image name)

problem: "app ... waits for db" overstates what Compose does. depends_on only starts services in order; it does not wait until the database is ready to accept connections unless a health-check condition is set.
fix: Compose starts db before app, but does not wait for the database to be ready. Add a health check with a depends_on condition, or make the app retry the connection.

problem: "A registry is a private image store" is too narrow — registries such as Docker Hub are public by default; the key contrast with Git is what they store, not their visibility.
fix: A registry stores images (public or private), not source commits like a Git repository.
